mainTopic: Aggadah on acquiring Torah and ה''s patience; the size limit of פסי ביראות and whether a public road ruins partitions
overview: This amud opens by finishing an aggadic reading of 'שחורות כעורב' about who truly holds on to Torah. The answers are the one who learns from dawn to evening, and the one who suffers hardship for it (רבה). רבא adds the one who acts 'cruel like a raven' to his family for Torah, as רב אדא בר מתנא did. Next come derashos on how ה' repays the wicked quickly while delaying the reward of צדיקים, and why 'ארך אפים' is plural. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about the boards around a well (פסי ביראות). It asks whether רבי יהודה's limit of בית סאתים measures the well alone or the whole enclosed area. A ברייתא is brought, and the גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר differ about a long, narrow shape. Then a new משנה asks whether a public road through the boards ruins them. רבי יוחנן explains the חכמים's 'strength of partitions' without agreeing to it, and the גמרא resolves an apparent self-contradiction in both רבי יהודה and the חכמים. The amud ends with רבי יוחנן's ruling that ארץ ישראל has no Torah-level רשות הרבים, and אביי asks for the reason, which comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Torah is found in one who comes early and stays late
steps.stepSummary: The first explanation of 'שחורות כעורב' ends: Torah is found in the person who comes to the בית המדרש at dawn and stays until evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Torah is found in the one] who comes early and stays late for it in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: We are picking up in the middle of a sentence. The גמרא is finishing its first answer to 'in whom are the words of Torah found?': in someone who comes to learn at dawn and stays until evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'שְׁחֹרוֹת כָּעוֹרֵב' (black like a raven). The first reading plays on the sounds: שחורות sounds like שחר (dawn) and עורב sounds like ערב (evening). So the verse hints at a person who learns from morning until night.

keyTerms.meaning: gets up early, comes at dawn
for their sake (for the words of Torah)

phrases.english: who gets up early and stays late for their sake
phrases.notes: Continues a sentence from the previous daf: 'In whom do you find the words of Torah? In one...'

phrases.english: in the study hall.
phrases.notes: שחר and ערב are hinted at in the words שחורות and עורב.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמַּשְׁכִּים וּמַעֲרִיב עֲלֵיהֶן לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first answer, which began on the previous daf, to the question of how to read 'שחורות כעורב'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah stays with the one who learns from dawn (שחר) to evening (ערב).

steps.title: רבה: one who blackens his face for Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבה reads the verse as describing someone who makes his face 'black like a raven' through hardship and self-denial for Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: [Torah is found] in one who blackens his face for them like a raven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a second reading of 'black like a raven'. Torah is found in the one who goes hungry and suffers for it until his face looks darkened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading took 'black' as a sound-hint for the time of day. רבה takes 'black' literally, as the look of a person worn out by fasting and hardship. The focus moves from how many hours a person learns to how much he is willing to give up for Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: blackens his face (through hunger and hardship)

phrases.english: Rabba said:
In one who blackens his face
phrases.notes: He deprives himself, even of food, for learning.

phrases.english: for their sake, like a raven.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: בְּמִי שֶׁמַּשְׁחִיר פָּנָיו עֲלֵיהֶן כְּעוֹרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different reading of the same verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah stays with the one who endures hardship and self-denial for it.

steps.title: רבא: one who acts cruel like a raven to his family for Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the raven as a symbol of cruelty to its young. Torah is found in one who makes himself seem harsh toward his family so that he can learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: [Torah is found] in one who makes himself cruel to his children and his household, like a raven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third reading. The raven is known for not caring for its chicks, so Torah is found in someone who acts 'cruel' like a raven, leaving his family's needs aside to go learn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה looked at the raven's color. רבא looks at the raven's nature, since ravens were known to neglect their young. The point is that real Torah growth can require putting family comfort second for a time.
steps.confusionAlert: The word is מֵשִׂים עַצְמוֹ, 'makes himself' cruel. רבא does not praise real cruelty. He describes someone who chooses to look harsh by putting Torah ahead of household comforts.

phrases.english: Rava said:
In one who makes himself cruel
to his children and to the members of his household
like a raven.
phrases.notes: The raven was known to neglect its young.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בְּמִי שֶׁמֵּשִׂים עַצְמוֹ אַכְזָרִי עַל בָּנָיו וְעַל בְּנֵי בֵּיתוֹ כְּעוֹרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading, this time based on the raven's behavior instead of its color or the sound of its name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah stays with the one who puts learning ahead of his family's comforts.

steps.title: The story of רב אדא בר מתנא and the marsh reeds
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנא was leaving to learn. When his wife asked how she would feed the children, he answered that there were still reeds in the marsh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רב אדא בר מתנא, who was going to the study hall. His wife said to him: 'Your children, what should I do for them?' He said to her: 'Are the reeds in the marsh all gone?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story to show what רבא meant. רב אדא בר מתנא left for the yeshiva and told his wife to feed the children with marsh reeds if nothing else was available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wife's question is the natural family pressure that could stop someone from learning. His answer means the children will not starve, since there is still basic food like reeds, so he can go. This is exactly the 'raven-like' choice רבא described.

keyTerms.meaning: the yeshiva, the house of study

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of 'שחורות כעורב': (1) learning from שחר to ערב; (2) רבה: hardship that darkens the face; (3) רבא: acting 'cruel' to one's family for Torah, as רב אדא בר מתנא did.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא
phrases.english: Like this case of Rav Adda bar Mattana
who was going to the study hall,
his wife said to him:
Your children, what shall I do for them?
phrases.notes: How will I feed them while you are away?

phrases.english: He said to her:
Are the reeds in the marsh all gone?
phrases.notes: Meaning: they can eat reeds if there is nothing else.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבא's reading with an actual event.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading that one acts 'cruel like a raven' to his family for Torah.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of רב אדא בר מתנא and his wife.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי on God 'repaying to His face'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new verse. רבי יהושע בן לוי says that if the verse were not written, no one would dare say it, because it compares ה' to a person eager to throw a burden off his face.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And He repays those who hate Him to His face, to destroy them.' רבי יהושע בן לוי said: If the verse were not written, it would be impossible to say it. It is, as it were, like a person who carries a burden on his face and wants to throw it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic, a verse from דברים about how ה' punishes those who hate Him. רבי יהושע בן לוי explains the daring image the verse uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'To His face' suggests that the wicked are like a heavy load pressed against ה''s face, which He wants to push away quickly. Saying this about ה' would be too bold on our own, so רבי יהושע בן לוי stresses that only because the verse says it may we say it, and even then only 'כביכול'.

keyTerms.meaning: as it were (softens a bold description of ה')

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic, not part of the raven discussion. The verse is from דברים ז:י.

phrases.english: 'And He repays those who hate Him to His face, to destroy them,'
phrases.notes: דברים ז:י

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Were the verse not written,
it would be impossible to say it —

phrases.aramaic: כִּבְיָכוֹל כְּאָדָם שֶׁנּוֹשֵׂא מַשּׂוֹי עַל פָּנָיו,
phrases.english: as it were, like a person who carries a burden on his face,
and wants to throw it off himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁלֵּם לְשׂוֹנְאָיו אֶל פָּנָיו לְהַאֲבִידוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the raven discussion to a derasha on a different verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse describes ה' as eager to 'throw off' the wicked quickly, a bold image allowed only because the verse itself uses it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the principle that some descriptions of ה' may be said only because a פסוק says them, and even then softened with כביכול.

steps.title: רבי אילא: no delay for the wicked, but delay for the righteous
steps.stepSummary: From 'He will not delay for the one who hates Him,' רבי אילא infers that ה' does delay for the completely righteous. Their reward is held back for later.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He will not delay for the one who hates Him.' רבי אילא said: It is for those who hate Him that He does not delay, but He does delay for the completely righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילא reads the next words of the same verse closely. He infers that ה' does not delay paying the wicked, but He does delay paying the completely righteous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'no delay' specifically for 'those who hate Him'. That implies the opposite for the righteous. The wicked are repaid in this world, right away, for any good they did, while the completely righteous have their reward held back for עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: it is specifically [this] that... (introduces a precise inference)

steps.whatToRemember: Both derashos on the verse in דברים explain why the wicked can seem to prosper now: ה' 'repays' them quickly in this world, while the reward of the righteous is delayed for עולם הבא.

phrases.english: 'He will not delay for the one who hates Him,'
Rabbi Ila said:
It is for those who hate Him that He does not delay,
but He does delay for the completely righteous.
phrases.notes: Their reward is saved for עולם הבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יְאַחֵר לְשׂוֹנְאוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same verse in דברים, now its next phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repayment to the wicked comes without delay, while the reward of the completely righteous is delayed for עולם הבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a classic answer to why the righteous may suffer and the wicked may prosper in this world.

steps.title: Today is for doing, tomorrow is for reward
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading of 'היום לעשותם' supports רבי אילא's idea that the reward of צדיקים is held back for later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What is the meaning of 'which I command you today to do them'? Today is the time to do them, and tomorrow is not the time to do them. Today is the time to do them, and tomorrow is the time to receive their reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that matches what רבי אילא just said. ה' holds back the reward of צדיקים until later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'היום' (today) is read in two ways. First, this world is the only time to do מצוות. Second, the reward comes 'tomorrow,' in עולם הבא. That second reading is exactly the 'delay' רבי אילא described.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as (a link to an earlier idea)

steps.whatToRemember: This world is the time for doing מצוות. The reward is saved for עולם הבא.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹתָם״,
phrases.english: What is the meaning of the verse 'which I command you today to do them'?
phrases.notes: דברים ז:יא

phrases.english: 'Today to do them,' and not tomorrow to do them,
phrases.notes: There are no מצוות to do in עולם הבא

phrases.english: 'Today to do them,' and tomorrow to receive their reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אילא's claim that the reward of צדיקים is delayed
steps.raayaObject: רבי אילא's claim that ה' delays the reward of צדיקים
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading of 'היום לעשותם' (דברים ז:יא)

steps.title: Why the plural word 'אפים'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חגי (or רבי שמואל בר נחמני) asks why the פסוק says 'ארך אפים' in the plural instead of 'ארך אף.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חגי said, and some say it was רבי שמואל בר נחמני: What is the meaning of 'ארך אפים'? It should have said 'ארך אף'!
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher notices an odd word in the פסוק and asks about it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אף' means anger, so 'ארך אף' would simply mean 'slow to anger.' The פסוק instead uses the plural form 'אפים.' The question is what that extra, double form is coming to teach.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חַגַּי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chaggai said, and some say it was Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani:
What is the meaning of the verse 'long-suffering' (erekh appayim)?
phrases.notes: שמות לד:ו

phrases.english: It should have said 'erekh af' (singular)!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of ה' delaying, with another פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק uses the plural 'אפים'

steps.title: Patient with the righteous and with the wicked
steps.stepSummary: The plural teaches that ה' is patient in two ways: toward צדיקים and toward רשעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means ה' is long-suffering toward the righteous, and long-suffering toward the wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The question from the last step is answered. The double form means ה' shows two kinds of patience.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Toward צדיקים, ה' waits before paying their reward, as in steps 6 and 7. Toward רשעים, ה' waits before punishing them. One plural word holds both ideas.
steps.whatToRemember: 'ארך אפים' means two kinds of patience. ה' delays the reward of צדיקים and the punishment of רשעים.

phrases.english: Rather, He is long-suffering toward the righteous,
phrases.notes: He delays their reward

phrases.english: and long-suffering toward the wicked.
phrases.notes: He delays their punishment

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם לְצַדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural shows ה' is patient both with צדיקים and with רשעים

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה's בית סאתים limit include?
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה: does רבי יהודה's limit of בית סאתים measure the well together with the area inside the boards, or the well alone?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says, up to בית סאתים, etc. A question was asked: Does he mean the well together with the area enclosed by the boards, or perhaps he means the well without the boards?
steps.whatsHappening: The aggadic detour is over, and the גמרא goes back to the halacha of the משנה. It quotes רבי יהודה and asks what exactly his size limit measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first option, the whole area inside the boards may not be more than בית סאתים. In the second option, only the well itself is limited to בית סאתים, so the area inside the boards could be bigger. Step 11 explains the reasoning behind each side, and Steps 12-19 try to settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of two beit se'a (5,000 square אמות)
A question was asked before them
Upright boards set around a well in the public area

steps.confusionAlert: This is a real halachic question about measuring, not a challenge to רבי יהודה. Both options agree on the limit of בית סאתים. They only disagree about what is being measured.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר עַד בֵּית סָאתַיִם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: up to two beit se'a, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Did he mean the well together with the area of the boards,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא בּוֹר וְלֹא פַּסִּין קָאָמַר?
phrases.english: or perhaps he meant the well without the area of the boards?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בּוֹר וּפַסִּין קָאָמַר, אוֹ דִילְמָא בּוֹר וְלֹא פַּסִּין קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic section and returns to the halacha of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's בית סאתים limit applies to the whole enclosed area or only to the well itself

steps.title: The reasoning behind each side of the question
steps.stepSummary: Side one: a person focuses on his well, so no גזירה is needed. Side two: a person focuses on his enclosure, so we make a גזירה in case he confuses it with an oversized קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a person focus on his well, so that we do not make a decree in case he comes to carry in a קרפף larger than בית סאתים? Or perhaps a person focuses on his partition, and we do make a decree in case he comes to confuse it with a קרפף larger than בית סאתים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is spelling out the logic behind the two sides of the question it just asked about רבי יהודה's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people think of the enclosure as 'my well,' then only the well needs to be under בית סאתים, and nobody will mix it up with a big קרפף. If people think of it as 'my fenced area,' the whole enclosed space looks like a קרפף. So it must stay under בית סאתים, or people may start carrying in large קרפפות too.

keyTerms.meaning: sets his eyes on, meaning he mentally focuses on
an enclosed storage area behind a house that was not fenced in for living use; you may carry in it only up to בית סאתים
to confuse one case with another
his partition, meaning the enclosure made by the boards

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It explains the two sides of the question from step 10: well alone, or well plus the enclosed area.

phrases.english: A person sets his eyes on his well,
and we do not decree
lest he come to carry
in an enclosure larger than two beit se'a;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא, אָדָם נוֹתֵן עֵינָיו בִּמְחִיצָתוֹ,
phrases.english: or perhaps a person sets his eyes on his partition,
and we decree lest he come to confuse it
with an enclosure larger than two beit se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָדָם נוֹתֵן עֵינָיו בְּבוֹרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two sides of the question asked in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the person's focus on the well, so no גזירה is needed? Or is it on the enclosure, so a גזירה is needed because it resembles a קרפף?

steps.title: A ברייתא on how close and how far the boards may be
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the boards may be as close as a cow's head and most of its body. According to the תנא קמא they may be as far as a בית כור or two. רבי יהודה says up to בית סאתים is permitted and more is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: How close may the boards be? Enough for the head and most of the body of a cow. How far may they be? Even a בית כור, even two בית כור. רבי יהודה says: בית סאתים is permitted; more than בית סאתים is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. It sets out the basic disagreement between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The minimum distance is set so that a cow can fit its head and most of its body inside to drink. For the maximum, the תנא קמא allows a huge enclosed area, while רבי יהודה caps it at בית סאתים. The proof the גמרא wants does not come from these lines. It comes later in the ברייתא, from how רבי שמעון בן אלעזר words his view (see Step 16).

keyTerms.meaning: close: the minimum distance of the boards from the well
the head and most of the body of a cow, which sets the minimum space
short for בית כור, an area equal to 30 בית סאה (15 times בית סאתים)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
How close may they be?
Enough for the head and most of the body of a cow.
And how far may they be?
Even a kor, even two kor.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Two beit se'a is permitted;
more than two beit se'a is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to answer the question laid out in steps 10–11.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהודה measures the well alone or the whole enclosed area.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the minimum and maximum distance of the boards from the well.

steps.title: The חכמים challenge רבי יהודה from large pens and courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבי יהודה: don't you agree that a pen, a stable, a backyard, and a courtyard are permitted even at five or ten בית כור?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי יהודה: Do you not agree that a pen, a stable, a backyard, and a courtyard are permitted, even if they are five בית כור or ten בית כור?
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, the חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's limit by pointing to other enclosures that are allowed at any size. This sets up רבי יהודה's reply, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is this: if size does not matter for a pen or a courtyard, why should it matter here? The חכמים treat the area around the well like any other enclosed space. This exchange is part of the ברייתא being quoted. The גמרא's actual attempt to settle its question comes later, from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's wording (Step 16).

keyTerms.meaning: a stable or enclosure for animals
here, a backyard area behind the house
do you not agree? A challenge from a case the other side already accepts

steps.confusionAlert: Here מוּקְצֶה means a backyard. It does not mean the familiar שבת category of items you may not move.

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
Do you not agree
regarding a pen, a stable, a backyard, and a courtyard,
that even an area of five kor
or an area of ten kor
is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Inside the ברייתא, the חכמים challenge רבי יהודה's limit stated in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule that an area larger than בית סאתים around the well is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other enclosures (a pen, stable, backyard, or courtyard) are permitted at any size, so the well enclosure should be too.

steps.title: A real wall is different from corner boards
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers the חכמים: pens and courtyards have a real wall (מחיצה), while the well only has boards (פסין), so his size limit still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: That is a real wall, and these are only boards.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the challenge the חכמים raised in Step 13. He explains why big pens and courtyards are allowed while the boards around a well have a size limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pen, stable, backyard, or courtyard is surrounded by a full wall, which is a strong enclosure, so its size does not matter. The boards around a well are only corner pieces with large gaps between them. This weaker type of enclosure was allowed for a special purpose, so רבי יהודה limits it to בית סאתים.

keyTerms.meaning: A real, full wall or partition
Upright corner boards placed around a well, with open gaps between them

phrases.english: He said to them: This is a real partition,
phrases.notes: Refers to the wall around a pen, stable, or courtyard.

phrases.english: and these are only boards.
phrases.notes: The boards around the well are a weaker enclosure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: זוֹ מְחִיצָה, וְאֵלּוּ פַּסִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' challenge from Step 13 by distinguishing between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (real wall compared with boards)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If big pens are allowed, big areas inside boards should be allowed too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A real wall works at any size. Boards are a weaker enclosure, so they are limited to בית סאתים.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view on the size of the well
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says a well measuring בית סאתים by בית סאתים is permitted. The boards only need to be far enough from it for a cow's head and most of its body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: A well of בית סאתים by בית סאתים is permitted. The חכמים only said to place the boards at a distance large enough for a cow's head and most of its body.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more opinion, from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. He talks only about the size of the well itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, the measurement is of the well, which may be a square of בית סאתים by בית סאתים. He says the boards should not be pushed far out. They only need enough room for a cow to stand with its head and most of its body inside while drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of בית סאתים by בית סאתים, meaning a square shape
The head and most of the body of a cow

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹר בֵּית סָאתַיִם אַבֵּית סָאתַיִם — מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: a cistern of two beit se'a by two beit se'a is permitted,
phrases.notes: The measurement is of the well itself, in a square shape.

phrases.english: and they only said to distance the boards
phrases.notes: Distance the boards from the well.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כְּדֵי רֹאשָׁהּ וְרוּבָּהּ שֶׁל פָּרָה.
phrases.english: as much as the head and most of the body of a cow.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with another opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A well of בית סאתים by בית סאתים is permitted. The boards stand only a cow's length from it.

steps.title: Inferring that רבי יהודה measures the well and the boards together
steps.stepSummary: Because רבי שמעון בן אלעזר speaks only about the well, the גמרא infers that רבי יהודה must be measuring the well together with the area inside the boards.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי שמעון בן אלעזר spoke about the well and not the boards, this shows that רבי יהודה was speaking about the well together with the boards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from Step 10 using the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר must be saying something different from רבי יהודה. Since he clearly measures only the well, the גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה's בית סאתים includes the well plus the area inside the boards.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that he said

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִדְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: From the fact that Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said
the cistern and not the boards,
it follows that Rabbi Yehuda
was speaking of the cistern and the boards.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִדְּקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the opinion in Step 15 to try to answer the question from Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה measures the well together with the area inside the boards
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's wording in the ברייתא

steps.title: No: רבי יהודה also measures the well alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference: רבי יהודה was also talking about the well without the boards.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not so. רבי יהודה was speaking about the well without the boards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from Step 16. It says רבי יהודה is also measuring only the well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר mentions only the well does not force רבי יהודה to mean something different. Both could be measuring the well alone. This rejection sets up the next question, about how the two views differ.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so (a rejection of the previous idea)

phrases.english: But it is not so;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בּוֹר בְּלֹא פַּסִּין קָאָמַר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda was speaking of the cistern without the boards.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion drawn about רבי יהודה's measurement
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's wording does not prove that רבי יהודה includes the boards.

steps.title: Then the two views say the same thing
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה also measures only the well, his view seems identical to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection in Step 17. If both measure only the well, it is unclear what they disagree about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate opinions in a ברייתא should differ in some way. The rejection in Step 17 seems to erase any difference between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: If so,
that is the view of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה also measures the well without the boards
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both measure only the well, the two opinions seem to be the same.

steps.title: They differ over a long, narrow well
steps.stepSummary: The difference between them is a long, narrow shape. רבי יהודה allows it as long as the total area is בית סאתים. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires a square.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: a long and narrow shape.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing a practical difference between the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה only cares about the total area, so a long, narrow well of בית סאתים is fine. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said "בית סאתים by בית סאתים," which means the shape must be square.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר measure the well alone. They disagree only about shape: רבי יהודה allows a long, narrow area of בית סאתים, while רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires a square.
steps.confusionAlert: "בית סאתים אבית סאתים" does not mean a larger total area. It describes the shape: a square, with equal length and width.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
in a case that is long and narrow.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה permits it; רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires a square.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a practical difference between the views
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over a long, narrow well: רבי יהודה permits it, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires a square.

steps.title: A space used for living has no size limit
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives a general rule. Any enclosed space used for living, like a pen, stable, backyard or courtyard, is permitted for carrying even if it is huge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר stated a general rule: any enclosed space that is used for living, such as a pen, a stable, a backyard, or a courtyard, is permitted for carrying even if it is five or ten בית כור in size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a general rule from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about which enclosures may be carried in. This is the first half of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size limit of בית סאתים does not apply to every enclosure. If the enclosed area is actually used as a living space, it counts as a real private area no matter how big it is. Even five or ten בית כור, far larger than בית סאתים, is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: An open space whose purpose is living or dwelling
An animal pen and a stable
An area 15 times the size of a בית סאתים

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains where the בית סאתים limit comes from. The limit applies only to enclosures that are not real living spaces.

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar stated a general rule:
any enclosed space that is used for living,
such as a pen and a stable,
a backyard and a courtyard,
even if it is five beit kor in size
phrases.notes: Each בית כור is huge compared with a בית סאתים.

phrases.english: or ten beit kor, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view from the well case into a broad principle about enclosures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An enclosure used for living is permitted for carrying at any size.

steps.title: A structure that serves the outside area is limited to בית סאתים
steps.stepSummary: This is the second half of the rule. An enclosure made to serve the outside area, like a field hut, is permitted only up to בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And any structure that is used for the area outside it, such as huts in the fields, is permitted if it is בית סאתים, but forbidden if it is more than בית סאתים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר finishes his rule. Here he gives the opposite case, where the size limit does apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some enclosures are not built for living inside. They exist to serve the field or area around them, like a watchman's hut. These count as weaker private areas, so they are allowed only up to בית סאתים. The boards around a well (פסי ביראות) seem to fit this category, which is why they have a size limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A structure whose use is for the outside space, not for living inside
Huts or watchtowers in the fields

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two phrases. אֲוִיר שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ לְדִירָה is a space used for living, and it has no limit. דִּירָה שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישָׁהּ לַאֲוִיר is a structure that serves the outside, and it is limited to בית סאתים. The words are the same but reversed.
steps.whatToRemember: The size of the enclosure matters only when it is not a real living space. A living space may be any size. An enclosure that serves the outside area is capped at בית סאתים.

phrases.english: And any structure that is used for the space outside it,
such as huts in the fields,
if it is two beit se'a, it is permitted;
if more than two beit se'a, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל דִּירָה שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישָׁהּ לַאֲוִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the general rule by giving the contrasting case, where the בית סאתים limit applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An enclosure that serves the outside area is permitted only up to בית סאתים.

steps.title: A public road passing through the well enclosure
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. If a public road runs through the boards around a well, רבי יהודה says the road must be moved to the sides. The חכמים say this is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יהודה says: If a public road passes through the boards and cuts through the enclosed area, one must move the road to the sides. And the חכמים say: one does not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a dispute about a public road running through the area enclosed by the פסי ביראות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that if crowds walk through the enclosure, the boards stop working as a partition, so the road must be moved around it. The חכמים hold that the boards still count as a valid partition even with people passing through.

keyTerms.meaning: A public road, a path of the public domain
He must move it to the sides

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מַפְסַקְתָּן
phrases.english: if a public road was passing through them,
one must move it to the sides.
And the Rabbis say: he does not need to.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מַפְסַקְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on the same topic, the פסי ביראות, now asking whether a public road ruins the partition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה says the road must be moved aside. The חכמים say the enclosure is valid without moving it.

steps.title: This shows how strong partitions are
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both say that the חכמים's ruling shows how powerful partitions are.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both said: Here it informs you of the strength of partitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה. Two אמוראים explain what we learn from the חכמים's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though crowds walk right through the enclosure, the חכמים still treat the boards as a valid partition. This teaches that a partition keeps its legal power even when it does not physically stop people from passing.

keyTerms.meaning: The strength or power of partitions

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that a partition's legal strength does not depend on actually blocking traffic. This principle is important throughout מסכת עירובין.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar
who both said:
Here it informed you of the strength of partitions.
phrases.notes: This refers to the view of the חכמים in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the principle behind the חכמים's position in the new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, partitions keep their legal power even when the public walks through them.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן agree? His statement about ירושלים says no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן agrees that partitions override a public road. It challenges this from his own statement that walled ירושלים would be a רשות הרבים if its gates were not locked at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he mean that the חכמים said this here, and he agrees with them? But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: ירושלים, if its doors were not locked at night, one would be liable for carrying in it because it would count as a רשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן personally holds that partitions are powerful. It then attacks that idea with another statement he made about ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירושלים had walls all around it, which are partitions. Even so, רבי יוחנן said it would still count as a רשות הרבים if the gates stayed open, because of the many people passing through. That means walls alone do not beat a public road, which is the opposite of the חכמים's view in the well case.

keyTerms.meaning: And he himself holds this view
But didn't he say…? (introduces a challenge)
Public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In the well case the partitions are boards, and in the ירושלים case they are city walls. The shared question is whether partitions still work when many people walk through.

phrases.english: Here [the חכמים said it], and he agrees with it?
But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say
that רבי יוחנן said:
Jerusalem, were it not that its doors
are locked at night,
one would be liable for [carrying in] it as a public domain.
phrases.notes: So walls alone do not cancel public traffic.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן, וּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ? וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what רבי יוחנן's comment in Step 23 really means
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יוחנן personally agrees with the חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן said walled ירושלים would still be a רשות הרבים, so he holds that partitions do not override public traffic

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was only explaining the חכמים, not agreeing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן was explaining the חכמים's view in the well case without holding it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: here [the חכמים said it], and he does not agree with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by rereading רבי יוחנן's statement. He was describing what the חכמים hold, not his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words 'partitions are powerful' were an explanation of the חכמים's reasoning. In his own view, shown by the ירושלים statement, partitions do not override a public road. So his two statements no longer contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And he does not hold this view

phrases.english: Rather: here [the חכמים said it], and he does not agree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כָּאן — וְלָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן personally agreed that partitions override a public road
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן was only explaining the חכמים's reasoning and does not agree with it
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן explains the חכמים's 'power of partitions' reasoning, but his own view, as seen with ירושלים, is that public traffic beats walls.

steps.title: Announcing contradictions in both רבי יהודה and the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that each side's view in the well case contradicts another statement by that same side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And [the גמרא] raised a contradiction between one statement of רבי יהודה and another statement of רבי יהודה, and between one statement of the חכמים and another statement of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: This line prepares the next move. The גמרא announces that both opinions seem to contradict themselves, and the source comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the well case, רבי יהודה said a public road ruins the partitions and the חכמים said it does not. The גמרא is about to show a ברייתא where each side seems to hold the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: And he raised a contradiction (threw one source against another)

phrases.english: And he raised a contradiction between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yehuda.
And he raised a contradiction between the Rabbis and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִי דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the dispute of Step 22 and opens a new contradiction challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of both רבי יהודה and the חכמים in the well case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side's view about public roads and partitions seems reversed in another source

steps.title: רבי יהודה: side posts can enclose a public road between two houses
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: someone with houses on both sides of a public road may put up side posts or cross beams at both ends and then carry in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Furthermore, רבי יהודה said: Someone who had two houses on two sides of a public domain may make a לחי on this side and a לחי on that side, or a קורה on this side and a קורה on that side, and carry in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for the contradiction. Here רבי יהודה lets weak partitions turn a public road into a place where carrying is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the well case, רבי יהודה said a public road ruins the partition made by the boards around the well. Here he says a simple לחי or קורה at each end is enough, even with people walking through. That looks like the opposite of his view by the well.

keyTerms.meaning: Side post placed at the opening of an alley
Cross beam placed over an opening

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:
One who had two houses
on two sides of the public domain,

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ לֶחִי מִכָּאן וְלֶחִי מִכָּאן,
phrases.english: may make a side post here and a side post there,
or a cross beam here and a cross beam there,
and carry in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the contradiction announced in Step 26
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a לחי or קורה at each end of a public road between two houses permits carrying in the middle
steps.confusionAlert: Here it is רבי יהודה who is lenient about partitions over a public road, which is the reverse of his strict position by the well.

steps.title: The חכמים: a public road cannot be fixed this way
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה that a public road cannot be made fit for carrying with an עירוב like this.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: One does not make an עירוב for a public domain in this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's leniency. This finishes the source and sets up the full contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the well, the חכמים said partitions are strong enough to override a public road. Here they say side posts cannot fix a public road. So both sides seem to switch positions, and the גמרא will need to explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not make an עירוב (make an area fit for carrying)

phrases.english: They said to him: One cannot make an eiruv for
the public domain in this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מְעָרְבִין רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא with the חכמים's response, which completes the contradiction
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, side posts or beams cannot permit carrying in a public road
steps.whyThisMatters: Together with Step 27, this shows that רבי יהודה and the חכמים seem to have switched positions compared with the well case. The גמרא must now reconcile both sides.

steps.title: Each side contradicts itself
steps.stepSummary: After laying out the ברייתא, the גמרא states outright that רבי יהודה contradicts his own view and the חכמים contradict theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: So there is a contradiction between one statement of רבי יהודה and his other statement, and a contradiction between one statement of the חכמים and their other statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now formally states the double contradiction it announced in Step 26. It has finished quoting the ברייתא and is lining up the problem that it will solve next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the well case (פסי ביראות), רבי יהודה says a public road ruins the boards, so the road beats the partitions. In the ברייתא about houses, he says partitions make the road usable, so the partitions beat the road. The חכמים take the opposite side in each case, so each group seems to flip.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים, the majority of Sages

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful to keep the sides straight. In the well case רבי יהודה is strict (the road ruins the boards). In the houses case he is lenient (the partitions fix the road). The חכמים take the reverse position each time.

phrases.english: There is a contradiction of Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: His view in the well case versus his view about the houses.

phrases.english: and a contradiction of the Rabbis against the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The same flip appears on the side of the חכמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the ברייתא in Steps 27-28 and turns it into the contradiction announced in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of both רבי יהודה and the חכמים across the well case and the houses case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side seems to hold that partitions override a public road in one case but not in the other.

steps.title: Real walls versus boards for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה is consistent: houses are two real walls that can override a road, but well-boards are not real walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no contradiction between the two statements of רבי יהודה. There, with the houses, there are two proper walls. Here, with the well-boards, there are not two proper walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves רבי יהודה's contradiction by showing that the two cases have different kinds of partitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rows of houses on both sides of the road are solid, real walls. Two real walls are enough to make a separate area, so they can override the road. The corner boards around a well are only weak, partial partitions, so they cannot stand up against a public road passing through.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here (pointing to the two cases being compared)

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult:
There, there are two proper partitions.
phrases.notes: "There" means the houses on both sides of the road.

phrases.english: Here, there are not two proper partitions.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the boards around the well.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction in Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the quality of the partitions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to flip on whether partitions can override a public road.
steps.terutzMaskana: Real walls (houses) override a road; weak boards do not.

steps.title: Four walls in name versus only two for the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are consistent: well-boards count as four walls in name, while houses give only two walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is also no contradiction between the two statements of the חכמים. Here, with the well-boards, there is the name of four walls. There, with the houses, there is not the name of four walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the חכמים's contradiction using a different factor: how many sides the partitions cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each corner piece of the well-boards stretches along two sides, so all four sides have some partition. That counts in name as four walls, and four walls can override a road. The houses close off only two sides, which is not strong enough to override a public road.

keyTerms.meaning: The name or status of four partitions, even if they are not complete

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the order switches compared to the previous step, but the meanings do not. Step 30 mentions "there" (the houses) first, and this step mentions "here" (the well-boards) first. In both steps, "here" means the well-boards and "there" means the houses.
steps.whatToRemember: Each side is consistent, but for a different reason. רבי יהודה cares about how real the walls are. The חכמים care about whether there are four sides.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is also not difficult:
Here, there is the name of four partitions,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the boards around the well.

phrases.english: there, there is not the name of four partitions.
phrases.notes: "There" means the houses, which close off only two sides.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the contradiction in Step 29, which closes the cycle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the number of sides enclosed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים seemed to flip on whether partitions can override a public road.
steps.terutzMaskana: Four walls in name override a road; two real walls alone do not.

steps.title: No Torah-level public domain in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר יוסף quotes רבי יוחנן: one is not liable for carrying in a רשות הרבים in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: In ארץ ישראל, one is not liable for carrying in a public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching, quoted in the name of רבי יוחנן. It says that ארץ ישראל does not have a public domain that carries Torah-level liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling claims that something about the whole land takes away liability for carrying in its public areas. This is surprising, because Step 25 concluded that רבי יוחנן himself holds that walls do not override public traffic, as with ירושלים. The reason for the ruling is asked in the next step, and the answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: One is not liable (no Torah-level punishment or קרבן)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean carrying in ארץ ישראל is allowed. It only means there is no Torah-level liability. Rabbinic restrictions can still apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling affects the status of every public area in an entire country, so it has wide effects on the laws of carrying.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The Land of Israel, one is not liable in it
on account of the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching connected to the theme of partitions versus a public domain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל there is no Torah-level liability for carrying in a רשות הרבים.

steps.title: אביי asks for the reason
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי repeats רבי יוחנן's teaching, and אביי asks him what the reason is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי sat and taught this teaching. אביי said to רב דימי: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes רב דימי teaching רבי יוחנן's ruling, and אביי asking him to explain it. This sets up the explanation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is not attacking the ruling. He is asking for the reason behind it. The ruling is surprising, because ארץ ישראל clearly has crowded public roads, so some special factor must remove the liability.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi sat
and was saying this teaching.
Abaye said to Rav Dimi:
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב דִּימִי מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in Step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why there is no Torah-level רשות הרבים in ארץ ישראל.
